Codex review: needs real behavior proof before merge. ## What this changes This PR adds OpenClaw ID tunnel transport, local account sign-in, and membership-bound Gateway authentication and scheduled execution. **Example:** An admitted viewer connects through the OpenClaw ID tunnel to a token-authenticated Gateway. - **Before:** Current main has membership authority but no working tunnel entrance. - **After:** The viewer can read through the tunnel without the Gateway token, while chat and administrative operations remain denied. ## Review scores | Measure | Result | What it means | |---|---|---| | **Overall readiness** | 🦐 gold shrimp **(3/6)** | Useful, owner-directed implementation with the previous blocker repaired; partial Gateway evidence does not yet establish every retained-authority or upgrade boundary. | | **Proof confidence** | 🦐 gold shrimp **(3/6)** | Real behavior proof is necessary before merge. See [Before merge](#before-merge). | | **Patch quality** | 🦐 gold shrimp **(3/6)** | Security review found an item that needs attention. | ## Product **Kind:** Feature · **Worth it:** Yes · **Fix scope:** Complete **User problem:** Owners and members cannot reach a linked Gateway through the OpenClaw ID relay using their admitted browser devices. **Reason:** Maintainer direction approves the capability and durable-device authority model, while existing access methods and the default-disabled Labs boundary remain available. ## Merge readiness ⛔ **Blocked before merge - 3 items remain** Keep this maintainer-authored feature open. The previous protocol revocation finding is resolved, and no additional concrete correctness defect was established. **Priority:** P2 **Reviewed head:** `c546781a4b318e823d0786e1402c6e3990ba56a1` ## Before merge - [ ] **Add real behavior proof** - Authority-chain proof required: the current-head Gateway trace establishes legitimate enrollment, private-ingress rejection, delegated-device teardown, and refused reconnects and token reuse. It does not show refusal before a held HTTP tool effect, ordinary-ingress token replay after a Labs-disabled restart, or cold-restored jobs and streams after removal, reapproval, or role change. Those paths have supporting tests, and the maintainer explicitly accepted the recorded trace limitation, but that does not waive this review's final-effect gate. Supply redacted production-path output with allowed controls and forbidden effects absent; redact IPs, API keys, phone numbers, and non-public endpoints. After adding proof, update the PR body, then request a new review with `@clawsweeper re-review`. The PR author or someone with repository write access can request it. - [ ] **Resolve security review attention item** - No additional concrete exploit was established, but required final-effect authority evidence remains incomplete. - [ ] **Add data-model compatibility proof** - The review found that existing stored data may not work after upgrade. Show that existing data still loads and works with this change. ## Findings None. ### Tests - Low-value test `src/gateway/openclaw-id/tunnel-principal.test.ts`: Remove the 'caps members by role and leaves owners uncapped' helper test: it asserts static policy values already exercised through owner, operator, and viewer Gateway authorization scenarios. - Missing end-to-end proof: Supply production-path allowed/refused final-effect evidence for held HTTP execution, disabled-restart token replay, and cold-restored jobs and streams; stable-to-head preservation is also unshown.
Agent review details ### How this fits together The tunnel authenticates device keys and forwards HTTP and WebSocket traffic through private ingress; Gateway membership and execution owners determine permissions and revalidate retained device grants. ```mermaid flowchart LR Browser[Admitted browser device] --> Tunnel[QUIC tunnel child] Tunnel --> Ingress[Private Gateway ingress] Ingress --> Auth[Gateway authentication] Auth --> Membership[Membership authority] Auth --> Execution[HTTP and WebSocket execution] Execution --> Scheduled[Scheduled work and recovery] Scheduled --> Membership ``` ### Technical review Best possible solution: Retain the existing membership and execution owners, with device-bound grants verified through their final effects and existing persisted state preserved. Do we have a high-confidence way to reproduce the issue? This is a new capability: current main provides membership authority but lacks the tunnel entrance that this PR supplies. Is this the best way to solve the issue? The design reuses the membership, authentication, admission, and recovery owners; separating transport custody from membership decisions and retaining process grants independently of mutable payloads serves distinct lifecycle requirements. AGENTS.md: found and applied where relevant. Codex review notes: model internal, reasoning medium; reviewed against [8dd41fc95291](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/8dd41fc95291553e5885fec09992bd41c3038004). ### Provenance checked - `OpenClaw ID service and admission` keeps the original intent (428ca7daffc9b805a865700012cae906ae316071: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/192335 deliberately landed membership authority without transport and deferred linking until the tunnel stage.) - `Scheduled operator-source retention` changes intended behavior with a stated reason (d74a4aeb7d62362234570f2e8245830f5edae49f: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/176422 retained bounded authenticated authority for conversation continuations; the current PR explicitly extends device-bound retention to independent scheduled work.) - `Restart recovery and role ceilings` keeps the original intent (56753f7762a72df6d982f2158febc7c7db9a46bd: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/193098 preserves original authority and current policy across recovery; the new device source uses the same recovery owner and adds membership revalidation.) ### Testing Proof path: in-process harness. ### Security Needs attention: No additional concrete exploit was established, but required final-effect authority evidence remains incomplete. ### Evidence What I checked: - **Maintainer direction and accepted tradeoffs:** The complete PR body records owner decisions to retain device authority for durable work and accept the supplied Gateway trace with named remaining proof limitations. The current-head security guard independently identifies the author as a repository administrator; no additional product-direction approval is needed. ([c546781a4b31](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/c546781a4b318e823d0786e1402c6e3990ba56a1)) - **Previous blocking repair included:** The reviewed head contains https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/193990, merged as c6480f78289d0d2cc02b03b0b2b3acea26b03012. The protocol now preserves approval lineage, restricts re-additions to the approver's subtree, and requires the certificate signer to match the current change signer. ([`packages/openclaw-id-protocol/src/authority/apply.ts:352`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/c546781a4b318e823d0786e1402c6e3990ba56a1/packages/openclaw-id-protocol/src/authority/apply.ts#L352), [c546781a4b31](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/c546781a4b318e823d0786e1402c6e3990ba56a1)) - **Retained authority checks:** HTTP authority incorporates current membership, and retained principals compare claw, root, listing sequence, owner-device identity, account, and role against the resident membership owner. ([`src/gateway/openclaw-id/tunnel-principal.ts:119`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/c546781a4b318e823d0786e1402c6e3990ba56a1/src/gateway/openclaw-id/tunnel-principal.ts#L119), [c546781a4b31](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/c546781a4b318e823d0786e1402c6e3990ba56a1)) - **Gateway proof and its limits:** The trace at https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/192345#issuecomment-6686314755 exercises private ingress, real membership storage, WebSocket admission, removal effects, and token revocation. The body reports its successful replay on the reviewed head and explicitly excludes held HTTP effects, disabled-restart replay, cold-restored work, and stable upgrades. Both downloaded screenshots were inspected; they show automation warning presentation rather than these authority scenarios. ([c546781a4b31](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/c546781a4b318e823d0786e1402c6e3990ba56a1)) - **Persisted-format boundary:** The recovery codec retains the parent-bound source shape and adds a standalone gateway variant; cron storage also retains a private stream process grant. Serialization and owner-level tests support compatibility, but the PR explicitly reports no stable-to-head upgrade run. ([`src/gateway/operator-run-recovery-source.codec.ts:80`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/c546781a4b318e823d0786e1402c6e3990ba56a1/src/gateway/operator-run-recovery-source.codec.ts#L80), [c546781a4b31](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/c546781a4b318e823d0786e1402c6e3990ba56a1)) - **Native transport contract:** The child executes the local iroh binding and requires its relay watcher. https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/193995 is included in the reviewed ancestry; its endpoint-owned cancellation ends the watcher when the endpoint closes. ([`crates/openclaw-iroh-node/src/endpoint.rs:154`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/c546781a4b318e823d0786e1402c6e3990ba56a1/crates/openclaw-iroh-node/src/endpoint.rs#L154), [c546781a4b31](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/c546781a4b318e823d0786e1402c6e3990ba56a1)) ### PR surface PR surface statistics unavailable: the file list is incomplete. ### Preflight source Source unknown. Source comparison at the observed PR snapshot only. Completion is self-reported; body, policy, tests, execution, and report bytes are not verified. ### Labels Label changes: - add `rating: 🦐 gold shrimp`: Overall readiness is 🦐 gold shrimp; proof is 🦐 gold shrimp and patch quality is 🦐 gold shrimp. - remove `rating: 🧂 unranked krab`: Current PR rating is `rating: 🦐 gold shrimp`, so this older rating label is no longer current. Label justifications: - `P2`: This is an optional Labs feature with meaningful remote-access value and no established urgent regression. - `merge-risk: 🚨 security-boundary`: The PR makes authenticated tunnel devices Gateway principals and persists their authority for later execution; ordinary CI cannot establish all final-effect revocation guarantees. - `rating: 🦐 gold shrimp`: Overall readiness is 🦐 gold shrimp; proof is 🦐 gold shrimp and patch quality is 🦐 gold shrimp. - `status: 📣 needs proof`: The PR needs real behavior proof before ClawSweeper can clear the contributor ask. ### Rank-up moves Optional improvements that raise the rating; they are not merge blockers. - Add final-effect proof for removed or reassigned devices on held HTTP requests and restored jobs and streams, including saved-token replay after a Labs-disabled restart. - Demonstrate a latest-stable-to-head upgrade preserving existing jobs, settings, and stored authority. ### Rating scale 6/6 🦀 challenger crab · 5/6 🦞 diamond lobster · 4/6 🐚 platinum hermit · 3/6 🦐 gold shrimp · 2/6 🦪 silver shellfish · 1/6 🧂 unranked krab. Overall follows the weaker of proof and patch quality; ✨ marks media proof (a screenshot, video, or linked artifact) that directly shows the changed behavior. ### Workflow ClawSweeper edits this one comment on every review. Comment `@clawsweeper re-review` for a fresh review only. Repair and merge execution lanes are retired. ### History

nodes.body: This is a hard need for me.

Proof for the P1 / high finding ("Include the protocol revocation repair before exposing tunnel statements"; "Surviving delegated membership grants Gateway owner authority").

The protocol repair, #193990, is now merged to `main` as c6480f78289d0d2cc02b03b0b2b3acea26b03012. This PR still needs `main` merged in to pick it up.

I ran one scripted scenario on two builds and compared them:

- **Without the fix:** this PR's head `4f86c5741e84` alone.
- **With the fix:** this PR's head merged with #193990's head `40441d9933f9`. The merge was clean.

The script is a throwaway and is not committed.

What the scenario uses:

- **Real:**
  - a Gateway server (`createGatewaySuiteHarness`, token auth, `gateway.openclawId.enabled`)
  - the OpenClaw ID service and authority over the SQLite claw store
  - this PR's private ingress listener: a Unix socket with a per-boot proxy token
  - the tunnel API (`POST /_openclaw-id/v1/statements`)
  - Gateway WebSocket auth for relayed devices
  - the removal effects wired at Gateway startup
  - device-token issuance, binding and revocation
  - root changes submitted as a local operator: loopback `openclawId.authority` `submit` with the Gateway token
- **Replaced:** only the QUIC tunnel child. Requests enter the ingress socket the way the child forwards them: proxy token plus authenticated peer-key header. Membership updates sent to the child are recorded.

| Step | This PR alone | This PR + #193990 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Ingress request without the proxy token | 403 | 403 |
| D1 approves D2 via tunnel API (legitimate) | 200 | 200 |
| R enrolls C as local operator (legitimate) | accepted | accepted |
| D2 Control UI WebSocket over the tunnel | admitted as owner (`operator.admin`), device token issued | same |
| D2 re-certifies itself via tunnel API | 200, `approved_by` **moves off D1** | 200, `approved_by` stays D1 |
| D2 adds its peer key to C via tunnel API | **200** | 403 `target_mismatch` |
| E replays its old R-signed certificate after a capability reduction | **200**, caps restored to all four | 403 `wrong_signer`, caps stay `["approve_device"]` |
| R revokes D1: removal summary | `devices: 1, connectionsClosed: 0` | `devices: 2, connectionsClosed: 1` |
| D2's open WebSocket | **stays open** | closed by the Gateway, code 1008 |
| D2 peer key in membership pushed to the tunnel child | **still admitted** | removed |
| D2 reconnects over the tunnel | **admitted as owner** | refused: "this device no longer has access to this claw" |
| D2 reconnects with its old device token | **admitted** | refused (same message); token store reports `token-revoked` |
| D2 reads `/_openclaw-id/v1/membership` | **200** | 403 `not_owner_device` |
| C connects (independent root device) | admitted | admitted |
| R re-enrolls D2 under `root` (recovery) | accepted | accepted; D2 is admitted again with a fresh Gateway device identity |

After recovery, D2's old Gateway device identity is asked to re-pair ("pairing required: device is asking for a higher role than currently approved"), because removal revoked that identity's paired tokens.

- the other items in the review: a held HTTP tool request after removal, saved-token replay after a Labs-disabled restart, cold-restored jobs and streams, and a stable-to-head data upgrade
- the QUIC child and relay network
- a browser or Service Worker
